# third_party: Vendored C infrastructure (Phase 3a)

The ARM64 assembly controller (`core/controller/asm/`, built by a parallel
task) drives this vendored C layer for protocol work. Everything here is
**arm64-only**: the controller rewrite is ARM-only, so all C targets carry
`target_compatible_with = ["@platforms//cpu:aarch64"]`. The default amd64
platform (repo `.bazelrc`) skips them as incompatible — the existing amd64 Go
controller never links the C layer and its production build stays green.

| Package | Target | What it is |
|---------|--------|------------|
| `//third_party/protobuf-c:runtime` | `cc_library` | Pure-C protobuf-c v1.5.2 runtime (`protobuf-c.c`), no protoc, no libprotobuf |
| `//third_party/protobuf-c:protoc_gen_c` | `cc_binary` | The protoc plugin that generates `.pb-c` codecs (codegen tooling) |
| `//third_party/containerd-api:codecs` | `cc_library` | Generated containerd API codecs (23 proto files -> 46 committed `.pb-c` files) |
| `//third_party/containerd-api:codecs_roundtrip_test` | `cc_test` | protobuf-c encode->decode->compare round trip |
| `//third_party/libwebsockets:libwebsockets_static` | `genrule` | Static server-only libwebsockets.a (H1 + WS roles) |
| `//third_party/libwebsockets:lws_smoke_test` | `cc_test` | Starts the LWS server, hits `/healthz`, echoes a WebSocket |

## Gate builds

```sh
bazel build //third_party:phase3a_gate --platforms=//tools/bazel:linux_arm64
bazel test  //third_party:phase3a_tests --platforms=//tools/bazel:linux_arm64
```

## Codegen (regenerating the containerd codecs)

The committed codecs in `third_party/containerd-api/codecgen/` are generated
by the pinned `protoc` 36.2 + the vendored `protoc-gen-c` plugin over the
pinned `containerd_api` v1.12.0 protos (all pins + sha256s live in
MODULE.bazel). To regenerate after bumping those pins:

```sh
bazel run //third_party/containerd-api:write_codecs \
    --platforms=//tools/bazel:linux_arm64
```

This runs `//third_party/containerd-api:codegen` (a genrule) and copies the
bazel-bin outputs back into the source tree. The genrule is deterministic —
pinned protoc + plugin + protos — so committed == regenerated byte-for-byte.

### Why the two patches on protobuf-c?

1. `protobuf_c_protobuf34_compat.patch` — upstream commit d39f001b. Replaces
   the 8 `FieldDescriptor::label()` call sites (removed in libprotobuf >= 34)
   with a `FieldLabel()` helper. Mandatory for libprotobuf >= 34; applied
   unconditionally (the helper is a no-op re-derivation for older versions).
2. `protobuf_c_proto3_optional_feature.patch` — declares
   `FEATURE_PROTO3_OPTIONAL` in `GetSupportedFeatures()` so protoc permits
   containerd protos using the proto3 `optional` keyword (images.proto,
   fieldpath.proto). protobuf-c encodes those fields with `LABEL_NONE`
   semantics, wire-compatible with proto3 optional presence.

### Build-time protobuf dev debs

`protoc-gen-c` links the trixie snapshot's static `libprotobuf.a` /
`libprotoc.a` (same snapshot.debian.org timestamp as the repo's `@trixie` apt
extension). They're extracted by `tools/bazel/deb_extract.bzl` into the
`@libprotobuf_dev_arm64` / `@libprotoc_dev_arm64` / `@protobuf_compiler_arm64`
repos, and `protobuf-c/protobuf-c.pb.cc` (the plugin's own options) is
generated by the matching 3.21.12 protoc so the generated C++ matches the
linked libprotobuf headers (protoc 36.2's C++ output would not).

### Why a repo rule for libwebsockets instead of http_archive?

The v5.0.0 upstream archive ships 12 self-referential `libwebsockets`
symlinks under `minimal-examples/embedded/` that loop back to the repo root.
Any whole-tree traversal (Bazel glob, cmake configure) hangs on them, and
Bazel's `patches` mechanism cannot delete a symlink. `tools/bazel/
tarball_strip_symlinks.bzl` extracts the archive and deletes the loops at
fetch time. The cmake genrule then builds the static lib with the
control-plane config (static only, no SSL/HTTP2/zlib/client, H1 + WS roles).
